units.text: INT. GLASSHOUSE CONSERVATORY - SUNSET
A Victorian palm house of iron and glass, tall as a cathedral.
Sunset floods the panes amber and rose.
Orchids hang in baskets; a stone fountain trickles into a lily pond.
Brass paths wind through ferns.
Everything is green, damp, and gold.
CORALIE DUVERNAY, 30s, in a cream silk dress with a hem darkened by wet leaves, sits on the edge of the fountain, a folded letter in her lap.
Her dark hair is coming loose from its pins.
RAFAEL OYARZÚN, 30s, in a travelling coat, bag at his feet, stands at the end of the path, hat in hand.
His face is rain-streaked, though it has been dry all day.
At the far arch, hands clasped, stands SIGRID, 60s, Coralie's aunt, in black wool, severe, silver chignon.
You wrote that you were leaving.
units.name: RAFAEL

units.text: I wrote that I was thinking of it.
units.name: CORALIE

units.text: She wrote nothing of the sort. I wrote it.
units.name: SIGRID

units.text: Aunt Sigrid!
units.name: CORALIE

units.text: Someone had to.
units.name: SIGRID

units.text: Then you weren't thinking of it.
units.name: RAFAEL

units.text: I was. I am. I don't know.
units.name: CORALIE

units.text: She knows.
units.name: SIGRID

units.text: Let me speak!
units.name: CORALIE

units.text: Please.
units.name: RAFAEL

units.text: She has had a year to speak.
units.name: SIGRID

units.text: And you had a year to come back.
units.name: CORALIE

units.text: I was detained.
units.name: RAFAEL

units.text: For a year?
units.name: CORALIE

units.text: For eleven months. The last was spent walking.
units.name: RAFAEL

units.text: He expects pity.
units.name: SIGRID

units.text: I expect nothing.
units.name: RAFAEL

units.text: Then why are you here?
units.name: CORALIE

units.text: Because I could not do otherwise.
units.name: RAFAEL

units.text: A silence.
The fountain murmurs.
Light falls through the glass in long copper bars, laying stripes across the three of them.
Sigrid sighs, drops her hands.
I will see to the tea.
units.name: SIGRID

units.text: She exits through the arch.
Her footsteps fade among the ferns.
Coralie rises.
Smooths the letter against her skirt, folds it once more, and lets it fall into the lily pond, where it floats, bleeding blue ink.
There. Now we have nothing to argue about.
units.name: CORALIE

units.text: We never did.
units.name: RAFAEL

units.text: No. Only each other.
units.name: CORALIE

units.text: He takes a step.
She takes one.
They stop an arm's length apart.
The light goes out of the glass, rose to ash, all at once.
